new_exclusive_collateral.likely_pledging_entities_inferred: Not confirmed by 9fin as the specific pledging entities for this deal, but the Jan-2025 SSN offering memorandum's restricted-subsidiary schedule (doc 1f6d082c-4f6c-4790-aa86-7a28a8f06019, p.588) lists 'London Eye Holdings Limited' (co. no. 05686179), 'London Eye Management Services Limited' (02896849), 'Merlin Entertainments (SEA LIFE) Limited' (02182098) and 'Merlin Entertainments (Dungeons) Limited' (03671067) as existing group subsidiaries -- plausible candidates for where this collateral sits, flagged explicitly as an inference, not a 9fin-confirmed fact.

ranking_vs_existing_ssns_tlb.confirmed_by_sources: CONFIRMED, and stated as the headline characterisation: per Merlin's own 10-Sep-2026 press release, the New Term Facility 'will be secured alongside the Group's current senior secured financing' -- i.e. shares the pre-existing collateral pool with the SSNs and TLBs, consistent with a pari passu ranking on that pool. 9fin's 17-Sep-2026 article independently describes the new debt as sitting 'alongside its existing secured debt'. Separately, and also confirmed, the new facility benefits from exclusive security over the previously-unencumbered UK asset portfolio (London Eye, SEA LIFE London, Shrek's Adventure! London, UK Dungeons) that the SSNs/TLB do not have any claim on.
ranking_vs_existing_ssns_tlb.market_commentary_vs_confirmed_ranking: 9fin's 17-Sep-2026 article quotes buyside sources describing the resulting effect on the rest of the secured stack as being 'primed' by the Monarch/GoldenTree financing. This is qualitative market commentary about the economic/recovery effect of adding more secured debt plus exclusive collateral -- it is not itself a statement that the new facility has contractual priority (as opposed to parity) on the shared collateral pool.
ranking_vs_existing_ssns_tlb.pari_passu_or_senior_inference: INFERENCE, not confirmed by any 9fin source reviewed: the covenant mechanism identified below (Permitted Collateral Liens basket (b) in the SSN indenture) would allow up to the greater of GBP 601m / 100% LTM EBITDA of new secured debt to be granted 'super senior priority status in respect of the right to receive proceeds from an enforcement of the Collateral' -- i.e., priority in a waterfall, not just parity. The GBP 657m new facility is close to (modestly above) that GBP 601m/100% EBITDA cap, so if this specific basket was used, at least part of the new facility could in principle rank ahead of the SSNs/TLB for collateral enforcement proceeds. No 9fin news or document source reviewed states that this basket was actually the mechanism used, or that the new facility is contractually senior (rather than pari passu) on the shared collateral -- this remains CMCK's inference from covenant text cross-referenced against deal size only, and should not be read as a confirmed ranking.
ranking_vs_existing_ssns_tlb.exclusive_collateral: CONFIRMED: on the new UK asset portfolio, the new lenders have security with no equivalent claim available to existing SSN/TLB holders -- this portion is structurally exclusive, not merely pari or senior.

covenant_basket_permitting_transaction.source_document: USD 410m 7.375%/8.375% SSN indentures (2030/2031/2032 series), covenant basket text pulled via get_covenant_basket_texts, document_uuid 1f6d082c-4f6c-4790-aa86-7a28a8f06019 (2032s OM) -- broadly consistent language repeats across the 2030/2031 OMs per get_debt_instruments_and_covenants_table

relevant_baskets.name: Permitted Collateral Liens -- basket (b) (super senior capacity)
relevant_baskets.text_summary: Permits Liens securing Indebtedness under specified Ratio Debt / Credit Facility clauses, up to the greater of GBP 601m and 100% of LTM EBITDA, to be elevated to 'super senior priority status' for enforcement-proceeds purposes on the Collateral -- a fixed-capacity basket, not leverage-ratio-tested.
relevant_baskets.relevance: GBP 601m / 100% of the GBP 568m LTM EBITDA basis is very close to the GBP 657m new facility size, making this the most plausible mechanism for granting the new lenders priority on the shared collateral pool without breaching the indenture's ratio-based tests (see next basket).

relevant_baskets.name: Permitted Collateral Liens -- Secured Leverage Ratio test
relevant_baskets.text_summary: Additional secured debt on the Collateral pari passu with (or senior to) the SSNs otherwise requires the Consolidated Senior Secured Debt Ratio to be no greater than 4.75x.
relevant_baskets.relevance: Current gross secured leverage is already 5.7x (9fin cap table, 30-Jun-2026), i.e. above the 4.75x ratio test -- so a straightforward ratio-based incurrence of new pari/senior secured debt on the shared Collateral does not appear available, reinforcing the inference that the fixed-capacity super-senior basket above (not the ratio test) was the mechanism used.

relevant_baskets.name: Permitted Liens -- General Basket / Secured Leverage Ratio (for the NEW, non-Collateral UK assets)
relevant_baskets.text_summary: Liens on property that is not part of the indenture's defined 'Collateral' fall outside the Negative Pledge entirely and can be granted either under a General Basket (greater of GBP 181m / 30% LTM EBITDA) or subject to a 6.00x Consolidated Total Debt Ratio / 2.00x FCCR test.
relevant_baskets.relevance: Because the London Eye/SEA LIFE/Shrek's/Dungeons portfolio was previously unencumbered and outside the defined Collateral, granting security over it to the new lenders does not require any amendment to the SSN indenture's Negative Pledge -- it is a straightforward Permitted Lien on non-Collateral assets, which is consistent with the deal proceeding without a disclosed SSN indenture amendment or consent solicitation.

covenant_basket_permitting_transaction.consent_required: Not confirmed by 9fin sources reviewed either way. Based on the covenant basket analysis above, both legs of the transaction (super-senior capacity on shared Collateral, and a fresh Lien on previously non-Collateral assets) appear to fit within existing indenture/SFA basket capacity, which would mean formal SSN or TLB holder consent was not structurally required. This is CMCK's reading of the covenant text, not a 9fin-confirmed fact -- flagged explicitly as an inference. Likely source to firm this up: the closing documentation / any consent solicitation memorandum, once available on 9fin.

springing_maturity_on_ssns_tlb.existing_mechanism: Per 9fin's 09-Jun-2026 article ('Merlin hires Kirkland amid 2027 refi pressure', citing 9fin's own LME analysis), the existing senior secured debt carries a springing maturity covenant: all senior secured debt becomes current unless the 2027 SUNs are refinanced or repaid before 15-Jul-2027 (RCF) and before 15-Aug-2027 (TLBs and SSNs).
springing_maturity_on_ssns_tlb.does_this_deal_remove_it: Not yet confirmed post-close (transaction is not yet closed as of 28-Sep-2026; targeted for year-end 2026). If the new facility closes and repays the SUNs as intended, this should satisfy the springing-maturity condition and remove the risk of the RCF/TLBs/SSNs accelerating to current maturities in 2027. This is an expected outcome based on the mechanism as described, not a 9fin-confirmed post-close fact -- flagged as inference pending completion.

impact_on_unrefinanced_ssns.collateral_recovery_dilution: CONFIRMED: the new facility gains access to the existing shared collateral pool (pari passu on Merlin's and 9fin's own wording -- see priming_analysis.ranking_vs_existing_ssns_tlb) plus exclusive security over the new UK asset portfolio that SSN/TLB holders cannot access. Both effects dilute the SSNs'/TLB's relative claim on enforcement proceeds versus the pre-transaction position, even under a pari passu reading, simply because more secured debt (GBP 657m) now competes for the same collateral, and a further pool of assets sits entirely outside the SSNs'/TLB's reach. The additional possibility that the new facility also has priority (not just parity) via the super-senior covenant basket is an unconfirmed inference (see priming_analysis) that would, if true, worsen this dilution further.
impact_on_unrefinanced_ssns.secured_leverage_change: Gross secured leverage rises from 5.7x (current, GBP 3,240m / GBP 568m EBITDA) to an estimated 6.9x PF (CMCK calc, GBP 3,897m / GBP 568m EBITDA) once the new GBP 657m facility is added -- more secured debt now sits pari passu with (and, per an unconfirmed inference, possibly ahead of) the SSNs, competing for the same shared collateral plus the exclusive new UK asset pool.
impact_on_unrefinanced_ssns.maturity_profile: The new facility's stated 6-year tenor (~2032) sits roughly alongside/after the 2030-2032 SSN maturities, so it does not obviously mature ahead of the SSNs on its face. However, it carries its own springing maturity that could bring its due date forward to before 2030 if Merlin fails to refinance its debt -- the exact trigger (which debt, by what date) is not fully disclosed in the 9fin sources reviewed, so whether this could in practice pull the new facility's maturity ahead of, or keep it behind, the SSNs cannot be confirmed without the closing documentation.

Motion Bondco DAC sits alongside Midco as the issuer of the Existing Senior Notes (the 2027 SUNs) -- structurally outside the Senior Secured Notes Restricted Group.
